assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare bench-to-bedside arc: proglucagon-derived peptide biology, the insulinotropic role of GLP-1(7-36) amide, and degradation-resistant agonists that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits. Impact on patients and on metabolic physiology is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (receptor biology, proglucagon-derived peptides, translational mechanisms) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a defensible trio. Knudsen's pharmaceutical development of liraglutide/semaglutide is also decisive but is the fourth name; priority disputes around Mojsov's role versus others are not fully settled in my knowledge.
assessment.maturity: Large phase 3 outcome trials and real-world use confirm efficacy robustly and independently; the mechanism is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Choosing three from four credited names forces exclusion of Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose drug development contribution may be judged equal.
Credit for Mojsov's contribution versus other groups is contested and I cannot verify details independently.
Long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond, cell-type-specific control of neural circuits and has reshaped systems neuroscience, with extensions to cardiac, retinal and clinical applications including vision restoration. Originality and methodological reach are very high.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and demonstration of neuronal control and its adoption in behaviour (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenböck) all matter. A trio of Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth is plausible but leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, so allocation is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Thousands of independent studies over two decades confirm the tool; the interpretation of the discovery is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit; any trio leaves out major contributors, including Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
Whether the prize favours the discovery of the channelrhodopsins or the neuroscience application is uncertain.
Therapeutic translation is still early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and later PERK/ATF6 arms; it underpins understanding of ER stress in diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory cell physiology. Concept is clear, original and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central names credited, with Walter's laboratory identifying IRE1 and its role and Mori's laboratory the UPR element and signalling pathway. The pair is a natural and clean configuration, though Walter's work with Ron and others on PERK and ISRIB could prompt a wider claim; the supplied credit supports two.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed repeatedly across yeast and mammals and now entering drug development (ISRIB-type integrated stress response modulators). Fundamental discovery is mature; clinical translation is still partial.
uncertainties: Contributions of David Ron and Randal Kaufman are not in the credited names, so the pair may be seen as incomplete.
Therapeutic payoff remains largely prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created an entirely new class of living drugs. The concept, clinical proof and approvals make this one of the most transformative oncology advances of the past two decades.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and early design), June (clinical translation in CLL and CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early CD19 CAR clinical results) is a reasonable trio. Contributions by Zelig Eshhar, Dario Campana, Carl June's collaborators and others are not credited here and priority questions remain.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products, long-term remission data and many independent trials confirm efficacy. Limitations include toxicity, solid-tumour failure and access, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Eshhar-lineage work and the three listed names is debatable.
Durability across populations and long-term secondary malignancy risk are still being studied.
Rosenberg's inclusion could be judged secondary to the CAR-specific innovators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin discovery identified the neuropeptide system whose loss causes narcolepsy type 1, explaining a long-mysterious disorder and opening a path to orexin receptor agonists and antagonists. As a neurologist I value the clear link between molecular discovery, disease mechanism and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Yanagisawa and Sakurai identified orexins and their receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently found hypocretins; Mignot's canine genetics and human narcolepsy work established the disease link. Yanagisawa, Sakurai and Mignot span the discovery, receptor and disease pillars, but the simultaneous discovery makes de Lecea's exclusion sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Findings are replicated across species and clinical populations; dual orexin antagonists are approved for insomnia and agonists are in clinical trials. Interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Dual-discovery priority between the orexin and hypocretin groups and the choice of three of five names is contentious.
Orexin agonist therapy is still in late-stage development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR as the central regulator of cell growth and metabolism, discovered through rapamycin-resistant yeast mutants and extended to mTOR, links nutrient sensing to growth, ageing, cancer and immunosuppression. The discovery is foundational and broadly useful.
assessment.attribution: Hall is the clear central figure through the identification of TOR genes. Schreiber contributed rapamycin-FKBP12 target chemistry and mTOR identification in mammals (with Sabatini and Sabers/Brown groups). I exclude Sabatini given unresolved personal and institutional controversy and because Hall's core claim is distinct; other mTOR-pathway contributors such as Sabatini's mTORC subunits are not in a trio.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is extensively confirmed across eukaryotes with approved rapalogs in transplant and oncology. Maturity is high, though disease-specific therapeutic impact is narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether Sabatini and others deserve credit versus Schreiber is uncertain and my recollection of the details is not independently verified.
Credit divides between yeast genetics and the mammalian pharmacology, and possible wider recognition of rapamycin's discoverers (not in credited names) complicates allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined the cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway of innate immunity, bringing second messenger cGAMP and STING-dependent interferon signalling to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunology and ageing. The concept is novel and unifying.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the DNA sensor and messenger, the decisive discovery; Barber identified STING. The other names (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) contributed but are less likely to be prize-level. A pair of Chen and Barber is the cleanest allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is strongly replicated and mechanistically understood, but clinical translation (STING agonists, cGAS inhibitors) has not yet delivered approved therapies, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet demonstrated, which could make recognition premature.
Early STING work by others (Ishikawa/Barber versus Chen collaborators) leaves some priority ambiguity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation, particularly of the subthalamic nucleus and thalamus, produced a reproducible, reversible treatment for motor symptoms in Parkinson's disease and tremor, with clinical use in many thousands of patients and extension to dystonia and other indications. Impact for movement disorders is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's role in introducing high-frequency stimulation is central; contributions of Mahlon DeLong on basal ganglia circuit models and subthalamic targeting, and of others such as Pollak, are not among the credited names, so a one-person credit may be incomplete for a physiology-driven prize.
assessment.maturity: Strong randomised trial evidence and decades of use confirm efficacy; the field is mature. Whether the prize favours clinical technique over underlying physiology is an open committee question, and the committee knows this area well enough that I should be careful not to let that familiarity inflate the ranking.
uncertainties: Credit is limited to a single supplied name and the DeLong and other circuit-model contributions cannot be included.
Mechanism of action of high-frequency stimulation is still debated.
Prior major prize recognition for the technique is not something I can verify here.
